entries.claim: Noun class 1: prefix um- pairs with aba- (regular pairing)
entries.notes: Class 1 prefix um- for singular persons, regular pairing with Class 2 aba- for plural. Observed extensive use in corpus for people, agents, and some abstract concepts.

entries.claim: Noun class 2: prefix aba- pairs with aba- (regular pairing)
entries.notes: Class 2 prefix aba- for plural persons, regular pairing with Class 1 um- for singular. Extensively observed in corpus for groups of people.

entries.claim: Noun class 3: prefix um- pairs with imi- (regular pairing)
entries.notes: Class 3 prefix um- for singular objects, regular pairing with Class 4 imi- for plural. Distinguished from Class 1 by semantic category (objects vs persons).

entries.claim: Noun class 5: prefix i- pairs with ama- (regular pairing)
entries.notes: Class 5 prefix i- for singular objects and concepts, regular pairing with Class 6 ama- for plural. One of the most productive classes in the corpus.

entries.claim: Noun class 6: prefix ama- pairs with ama- (regular pairing)
entries.notes: Class 6 prefix ama- for plural objects, regular pairing with Class 5 i- for singular. Also used for ethnic groups like amaXhosa.

entries.claim: Noun class 7: prefix isi- pairs with izi- (regular pairing)
entries.notes: Class 7 prefix isi- for singular abstract concepts and tools, regular pairing with Class 8 izi- for plural. Highly productive class for abstract nouns and institutions.

entries.claim: Noun class 9: prefix u- pairs with o- (regular pairing)
entries.notes: Class 9 prefix u- for singular proper names and kinship terms, regular pairing with Class 10 o- for plural. Extensively used for personal names in corpus.
